description: Side-by-side reviews of smart home gear. Start with the system that runs your house, pick the protocol it speaks, then choose the switches, sensors, and locks that work on it.
data_source: Amazon product listings; each page carries its own data_captured date.
page_json: Every review page has a JSON twin at the same path with .json in place of .html.

protocols.name: Z-Wave
protocols.summary: Low-power mesh on a sub-GHz band, built for home automation and nothing else.

protocols.name: Zigbee
protocols.summary: Cheap, low-power 2.4 GHz mesh with the widest catalog of small sensors.

protocols.name: Wi-Fi
protocols.summary: Uses the router you already own. No hub, lots of bandwidth, lots of power draw.

protocols.name: Bluetooth
protocols.summary: Phone-to-device and short range. Easy to set up, hard to reach from outside the room.

protocols.name: Thread
protocols.summary: IP-based, self-healing 2.4 GHz mesh. The low-power radio behind most new Matter devices.

protocols.name: Matter
protocols.summary: A shared language, not a radio. Runs over Wi-Fi, Thread, or Ethernet and works across Apple, Google, Amazon, SmartThings, and Home Assistant.

protocols.name: Lutron Clear Connect
protocols.summary: Lutron's own RF used by Caseta and RadioRA. Proprietary and very reliable.

protocols.name: 433 MHz RF
protocols.summary: Simple one-way radio found in cheap sensors, weather stations, and remotes.
